hints: Focus on what makes propagation special, a free radical is used up as a reactant but a new free radical is made as a product to keep the chain going.
Write out the two propagation steps for $\text{CH}_4$ with $\text{Br}_2$ and notice which two radicals appear on the left hand side.
Now check termination, where any two radicals join together, and see which pair of radicals can both act as reactants in both types of step.
walkthrough:
**Recall the propagation chain**

Think of propagation as a cycle. One radical reacts, then it creates the next radical.

Initiation:
$$\text{Br}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{Br}^{\bullet}$$

Propagation 1:
$$\text{Br}^{\bullet} + \text{CH}_4 \rightarrow \text{HBr} + \text{CH}_3^{\bullet}$$

Propagation 2:
$$\text{CH}_3^{\bullet} + \text{Br}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{Br} + \text{Br}^{\bullet}$$

**Recall the termination steps**

Termination is the opposite. Radicals are removed when any two combine to make a stable molecule.

$$\text{Br}^{\bullet} + \text{Br}^{\bullet} \rightarrow \text{Br}_2$$
$$\text{CH}_3^{\bullet} + \text{CH}_3^{\bullet} \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_6$$
$$\text{Br}^{\bullet} + \text{CH}_3^{\bullet} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{Br}$$

**Apply both conditions to P and Q**

From Step 1, the only radicals used as reactants in propagation are $\text{Br}^{\bullet}$ and $\text{CH}_3^{\bullet}$. From Step 2, those same two radicals are both used as reactants in termination. So P and Q must be that pair.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{Br}^{\bullet}$ is correct, but H as an atom is not a chain carrier. The propagation steps use $\text{CH}_4$, not H, and produce HBr. There is no $\text{H}^{\bullet}$ radical reacting in propagation or termination.
options.B: Correct. $\text{Br}^{\bullet}$ is a reactant in propagation 1 and $\text{CH}_3^{\bullet}$ is a reactant in propagation 2, so both satisfy the first condition. Both also combine in termination ($\text{Br}^{\bullet} + \text{Br}^{\bullet}$, $\text{CH}_3^{\bullet} + \text{CH}_3^{\bullet}$, $\text{Br}^{\bullet} + \text{CH}_3^{\bullet}$), so both satisfy the second condition.
options.C: Incorrect. $\text{Br}^{\bullet}$ fits, but $\text{C}_2\text{H}_6$ does not. Ethane is a stable product of termination ($\text{CH}_3^{\bullet} + \text{CH}_3^{\bullet}$), not a radical reactant in propagation or termination.
options.D: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3^{\bullet}$ fits, but $\text{CH}_3\text{Br}$ does not. Bromomethane is the stable main product of propagation 2 and termination, not a radical reactant in either type of step.
